summary:
SlowBurn is an interactive global wildfire observatory web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspots. Using the NASA FIRMS Map Key API, it integrates live and trailing 1-year thermal detections from MODIS (Terra and Aqua, 1 km) alongside VIIRS (NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and Suomi-NPP, 375 m) across an interactive satellite map, fire activity analytics dashboard, and 12-month burning calendar.
Because VIIRS captures smaller 375 m pixels than MODIS’s 1 km grid, raw VIIRS hotspot counts often appear several times higher for the same wildfire. SlowBurn addresses this sensor discrepancy by computing a dynamic MODIS-equivalent harmonization scale and grouping nearby same-day detections (~5 km grid) into unified fire event clusters—while letting users toggle individual feeds, filter by Fire Radiative Power (FRP), confidence, day/night pass, country boundaries, or custom bounding boxes, and export clean CSVs.
Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS data is critical for separating true wildfire trends from sensor resolution differences, giving researchers, communities, and responders an accessible, consistent view of active global burning.
details:
SlowBurn is a full-stack satellite wildfire observatory that brings NASA’s MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active-fire feeds into one consistent web app.

What It Does & How It Works

  • Data Ingestion & Cleanup: A Node.js and Express backend pulls Near Real-Time (_NRT) and Standard Processing (_SP) Area CSV feeds from NASA FIRMS across four satellites: VIIRS NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi-NPP, and MODIS (Terra & Aqua). Because each instrument formats data differently, the backend standardizes MODIS’s 0–100 confidence scores with VIIRS’s l/n/h tiers, aligns brightness temperature columns, and pulls two UTC days filtered to a rolling 24-hour window so counts don’t drop to zero right after midnight UTC.
    • Satellite Map: Plots tens of thousands of hotspots over ESRI World Imagery, OpenStreetMap, and CARTO basemaps. Users can click country borders (world-atlas/d3-geo), draw custom bounding boxes, enter coordinates, and inspect time spans from 1 day up to 1 year back.
    • Activity & Intensity Analysis: Breaks down Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW) into severity tiers (<10, 10–50, 50–200, and 200+ MW), charts daily detections against mean FRP, compares harmonized vs. raw sensor counts, and includes a paginated hotspot table.
    • Burning Activity Calendar: Shows a trailing 12-month Year × Month grid with monthly anomaly percentages. Clicking any cell jumps straight to that region and month on the live map.
    • Nearby Scanner & Export: Includes a 10 / 25 / 50 km radius fire scanner around any coordinate and one-click filtered CSV exports.

Why It Matters & Intended Impact

  • Fixes Resolution Confusion: Helps researchers, journalists, and regular readers avoid mistaking a sensor switch from 1 km MODIS to 375 m VIIRS for an actual surge in wildfires.
  • No GIS Software Needed: Turns raw NASA CSV telemetry into something anyone can filter (by FRP, confidence, day/night pass, or region) and export right in the browser.
  • Local Situational Awareness: Lets people and local planners check active fires within 10–50 km of a town or nature reserve and see how intense they are in megawatts.

Tech Stack

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
  • Frontend: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS v4, React Router, Leaflet, d3-geo, topojson-client, world-atlas, Lucide Icons, Motion
  • Backend: Node.js, Express 4, tsx, dotenv (with in-memory/disk JSON caching and per-IP rate limiting)
  • Data & Hosting: NASA FIRMS Area CSV API, GitHub, Render

Design Choices

  • Shape + Color Encoding: Instead of piling up identical red dots where you can't tell which satellite saw what, each spacecraft gets its own color and shape (circle, diamond, triangle, square) set against a dark earth palette so thermal hotspots stand out clearly.
  • Calendar-to-Map Shortcuts: Clicking a month in the Burn Calendar passes the exact country bounds and dates straight into the map URL so you don't have to re-filter manually.
  • Colorblind Accessibility: Includes both an Ember palette and a colorblind-safe Viridis option in the Burn Calendar.

Constraints & Practical Trade-offs

  • Hosting & Storage Limits: Storing the full 6 GB bulk CSV archive wasn't realistic on a budget server, so the live app queries the NASA FIRMS API over a trailing 1-year window instead—though the backend is structured to support the full bulk archive later.
  • Protecting API Quotas: FIRMS_MAP_KEY stays strictly on the server, backed by response caching (15 minutes for NRT feeds, 24 hours for SP) and per-IP rate limiting so public traffic doesn't exhaust NASA's rate limits.
  • AI Disclosure: All custom patchwork artwork and backdrop illustrations are explicitly labeled as AI-generated, and AI coding tools were used during development, while 100% of the fire detection data comes directly from NASA FIRMS.
